conclusion: not-clean: nine Major lifecycle/WORM/TOCTOU findings; seven Minors deferred

findings.rationale: Byte mutation after SEAL is refused; path/symlink/media mutation in the same window is not. publish() writes member['relative_path'], not the sealed declared path.
findings.summary: produce() aliases caller member dicts, so post-SEAL path/type/media mutation publishes under a hostile path.

findings.rationale: A refused transition must not mutate the snapshot. Partial writes leave head SEALED while config.json is already stored.
findings.summary: publish() writes WORM members before the receipt CAS, so a later digest failure poisons storage and blocks retry.

findings.rationale: ADR-0123 requires verify retained bytes and decode those same bytes. Mutating published.sealed.parsed changes consume without touching the snapshot.
findings.summary: captured_bindings() decodes artifact.value from seal-time parsed JSON, not from verified retained bytes.

findings.rationale: Document mutation is refused; mutating _Frozen.port/consumer_input substitutes the captured port.
findings.summary: derive_consumer_port returns the stored frozen.port instead of recomputing ConsumerCapturedPort from the document.

findings.rationale: Capture must bind the exact publication receipt identity.
findings.summary: publication_receipt_sha256 is a subset hash, not the PUBLISHED receipt digest, and is omitted from CAPTURED/CONSUMED.

findings.rationale: Deleting PUBLISHED from the shared store still allows capture(); store and live chain diverge.
findings.summary: Live CAS reads in-memory _streams and ignores WORM receipt-store tamper until _recover.

findings.rationale: A session started as producer-run can produce as alice-producer and still be reused as the consumer run_identity.
findings.summary: Same-run refusal compares consumer identity to the producer dict, not the producer LaunchSession.

findings.rationale: Consumer B can CONSUME stream A; the CONSUMED actor_runtime is B.
findings.summary: captured_bindings accepts any open consumer session, not the session that opened the verified capture.

findings.rationale: Two independent flows make release(session_A) return B's identity.
findings.summary: release() returns the last captured stream_id in the broker, not this session's stream.

findings.rationale: Does not bypass ../, NUL, or absolute-path refusals already tested. Tighten if a filesystem provider lands.
findings.summary: _path_error allows newline and most control characters in member paths.

findings.rationale: Not a WORM bypass; require int and exact 1 later.
findings.summary: link_count is True is accepted because True == 1.

findings.rationale: Byte-exact WORM can be pinned when a real store lands.
findings.summary: _recover re-canonicalizes store bytes, so pretty-printed receipts still verify.
open_capture replay mints a second unread CapturedMemberHandle.

findings.rationale: Does not emit a forged CONSUMED receipt.
findings.summary: require() marks the input used before CONSUMED CAS, so a failed CAS deadlocks that bindings object.

findings.rationale: Runtime pinning is a later CAS-hardening concern unless F4 must pin measurements now.

findings.summary: end_session does not revoke consumer sessions; consume still works.
